analysis.title: CoStar Group (CSGP): CRE and multifamily data show a gradual revenue recovery with margin expansion supporting earnings growth
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on CSGP with a 12-month price target of $36 vs $30.20 price, 19.2% upside. The call rests on a gradual organic revenue recovery and margin expansion as the more visible earnings catalyst.

US CRE sales volumes rose 11% y/y to $101bn in 3Q 2026, led by industrial (+48%), with office +9% and retail +9%, while multifamily fell 8%. Rising rates could constrain further gains through financing costs and a wider bid-ask spread.
Overall CRE volumes are at 94% of pre-COVID levels. Industrial is at 177%, retail 126%, multifamily 77% and office 55%, so the recovery is uneven.

CoStar Suite organic growth slowed to 8.1% y/y in 3Q 2026 from 8.6% in 2Q, below its 9.8% 10-year average. Sales headcount is down about 10% y/y, limiting new bookings. GS forecasts 7.0% in 4Q 2026, 8.1% in 2026, 8.8% in 2027 and 10.3% in 2028.

US multifamily vacancy fell from a peak of 8.5% in 4Q 2025 to 7.9% in 3Q 2026. CoStar forecasts 7.6% by 4Q 2027 as deliveries fall from 447k to 303k. GS expects this to support Apartments.com budgets and reduce ad-tier downsell.

Apartments.com organic growth slowed to 6% y/y in 3Q 2026 from 9% in 2Q and 10% in 1Q, well below its 17% 10-year average. Causes are customer cost-cutting, competitor pricing, small-property cancellations and weak sales capacity. CoStar guides to mid-single digits in 4Q 2026.

Apartment completions were 534k in 2025 and are forecast at 425k in 2026 and 303k in 2027, a 43% cut from 2025. Units under construction are down 33% from the July 2023 peak to 674k, and authorized units are down 25% to 120k. Both remain above long-term averages.

GS forecasts total organic revenue growth of 7.7% in 2026, 8.5% in 2027 and 10.5% in 2028. It cut 2028 revenue by 2.7% (organic growth by 230 bps) on a more measured Residential recovery, with Residential 2028 revenue cut 4.4%.

EBITDA margin is forecast to rise from 13.6% in 2025 to 22.1% in 2026, 24.3% in 2027 and 26.5% in 2028 (unchanged). 3Q 2026 EBITDA margin was 24%, up about 10 points y/y on lower Homes.com investment.

CoStar expects 2026 expenses ex-Zonda to land $150mn below plan and has identified at least $200mn of further efficiencies over 12-18 months. GS forecasts EPS growth of 60% in 2026, 18% in 2027 and 20% in 2028.
Annualized net new bookings fell 56% y/y in 3Q 2026. GS sees the bookings recovery as the key determinant of whether organic growth returns to double digits by 2028.
Company targets a 2025-2028 revenue CAGR of about 15% and $1.25bn EBITDA in 2028. Longer term it targets $2.3bn EBITDA at a 35% margin in 2030, which management calls conservative.
The price target of $36 uses 19.0x NTM+1YR EPS of $1.88 ($1.92 prior), a premium to the Info Services peer median of 15.9x. The stock is down 55.1% over 12 months (59.0% relative to the S&P 500).

market_movers.rationale: Margin expansion supports EPS growth, with upside from bookings and Homes.com monetization balanced against higher rates and delayed sales productivity. Target held at $36 and the 2028 revenue estimate was cut 2.7%.

sector_views.rationale: Buy on CSGP given improving CRE activity, normalizing multifamily vacancy and cost-driven margin expansion.

earnings_insights: GS FY2026E adjusted EPS $1.40 (unchanged, GS estimate), FY2027E $1.64 (prior $1.65), FY2028E $1.97 (prior $2.03). FY2025 adjusted EPS was $0.87 as reported.
GS FY2026E revenue $3,762mn (unchanged, GS estimate), FY2027E $4,185mn (prior $4,211mn), FY2028E $4,623mn (prior $4,752mn). FY2025 revenue was $3,247mn as reported.
GS adjusted EBITDA estimates: FY2026E $830mn (Exhibit 8, $839mn in summary table), FY2027E $1,015mn, FY2028E $1,224mn. 4Q 2026E adjusted EPS $0.48 and revenue $988mn are GS estimates.
Company 2026 revenue growth guidance is 16% at the midpoint. 3Q 2026 EBITDA margin printed at 24%, up about 10 points y/y.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Recovery continues but moderated from 16% in 1Q, and rising rates are a headwind.
Down from 8.5% peak in 4Q 2025 and still about 1.4 standard deviations above the 25-year average of 6.9%.
CoStar forecast of gradual normalization as deliveries fall.

trade_ideas.description: Long CSGP equity, Buy rating, 12-month price target $36
trade_ideas.rationale: Margin expansion drives healthy EPS growth while CRE and multifamily data point to a gradual revenue recovery.
trade_ideas.risk: CRE slowdown, macro deceleration, competition, slow residential uptake, margin shortfall from residential investment, integration risk.

risk_factors: Slow customer uptake of residential offerings
Margin shortfall from elevated residential investment
Higher interest rates constraining CRE transactions
Delayed sales productivity and rebuilding of sales headcount

Exhibit 5 shows multifamily units under construction against an average of 483K.

tension_points.bull_case: Margin expansion from 14% to 26.5% by 2028, $200mn of identified efficiencies and a recovering CRE and multifamily backdrop support EPS growth of 60%, 18% and 20%.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates, a 10% sales headcount decline and a 56% y/y drop in net new bookings could delay the organic growth recovery. Renewed investment or slower revenue growth would threaten margins.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure of bookings to improve sequentially from the 3Q low, or slower revenue growth or renewed investment undermining the margin trajectory.

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower Residential investment, operating leverage and cost efficiencies should expand EBITDA margins from 14% in 2025 to 26.5% in 2028.
theme_stances.evidence: margin expansion providing the more visible earnings catalyst

theme_stances.key_argument: Falling apartment deliveries should lower vacancy and improve Apartments.com customer economics.
theme_stances.evidence: multifamily vacancy declined from 8.5% in 4Q 2025 to 7.9% in 3Q 2026
